scenario: Local issuer policy and durable historical receipts for exact native write permits

stages.label: exact-issuer-policy-and-separate-keys
stages.explanation: A sixth write job has an explicit catalog and one claimed lease. Two owner-created local issuers have separate administrator credentials and immutable exact rules; the main policy covers three phases, while the other names a different worker. No person or model identity is established.

stages.label: credential-and-policy-gated-fill
stages.explanation: Wrong administrator credentials, an unlisted principal and a nonmatching worker policy refuse before new child directories are reserved. The holder credential does not administer issuance. A permitted fill creates a fresh native permit and a separate durable issuance receipt, then native protected execute reaches only ready.

stages.label: durable-issuance-reply-recovery-and-no-adoption
stages.explanation: The actual complete link issuance response is discarded after success and recovered exactly from its completed receipt. Changed holder credentials, principal, operation, action, permit or issuer conflict. A fresh issuance cannot adopt an already existing native permit. Native protected execution then performs only ready-to-linked.

stages.label: revocation-stops-new-issuance-preserves-native-permits
stages.explanation: Both issuers are irreversibly revoked. New issuance refuses, while exact historical issuance replay remains fixed after current administrator authentication. Exact create/revoke replay never reactivates the issuer. The previously issued finish permit still performs linked-to-completed with its own holder credential.

stages.label: historical-receipts-with-eleven-bindings-absent
stages.explanation: After lease release, an existing native permit still returns its cached protected finish result while four live bindings are absent. With three native permits and three actions also absent, exact completed issuance replay uses the live revoked issuer and administrator credential. Hiding the issuer makes eleven absent paths; own receipt lookup still reads only its controls. Every path returns in finally.

stages.label: exact-inputs-and-unchanged-domain-history
stages.explanation: Duplicate rule IDs and duplicate exact scopes refuse without reserving an issuer. Another revocation operation conflicts. Five earlier write jobs, released lease heads and three blocked restore jobs preserve their observations. Two issuers retain revocation, three durable issuance receipts and three active native permits retain history, and the new write remains completed.

limits: The owner bootstraps immutable local issuer policies. Administrator, principal and worker are self-declared labels; a bearer proves local possession, not a person, organization, independent model or semantic authority.

Rules match an exact principal, captured worker, ledger ID, index and PRE/POST phase pair. They contain no wildcard or priority and do not constrain lease generation; every native permit still captures its exact original action and claim.

New issuance requires the live issuer credential, an unrevoked issuer and a matching explicit rule. The issuer, issuance, native permit and action locks share one deadline. Issuance itself performs no write phase and does not renew a lease.

A separate immutable issuance receipt follows the durable native grant. Their directories do not form an atomic transaction; a failure between writes may leave a native permit usable through the old API without a completed issuance receipt. Such partial states are not repaired or adopted here.

Issuer revocation blocks future issuance and waits behind admitted issuing. Existing native permits remain independent; their own bearer executes or self-revokes them. Old APIs, other issuers, filesystem owners and copies remain outside this managed issuance policy.

An exact complete issue replay authenticates the live issuer and holder request but returns immutable history even after issuer revocation, without reading child permits or actions. Own receipt lookup needs only its own controls and does not establish current issuer or child permission.

The actual complete link issuance reply was discarded and recovered exactly without new controls. This ordinary workflow does not demonstrate process overlap, issuance/revoke races, partial writes, interrupted receipt sealing, power loss, expiry waits or clock regression.

Eleven paths are temporarily absent at the widest observation: issuer, three native permits, three actions and four live bindings. All return in finally. Receipt lookup neither reconstructs missing private bodies nor repairs historical directories.

The driver reads validated public responses, private credential markers and lstat metadata, never private control bodies, SQL rows or staging. The earlier source/live histories remain R4/36 and R5/59; no archival, deletion, external LLM or semantic approval is performed.
